name: Familial Cutaneous Collagenoma

criteria.description: Presence of multiple asymptomatic, firm, skin-colored to hypopigmented nodules predominantly on the trunk and upper arms
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Skin biopsy demonstrating increased dense collagen bundles with decreased elastic fibers in the dermis
No evidence of systemic connective tissue disorders or associated syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple characteristic cutaneous nodules with histopathological confirmation and a positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology and family history; genetic testing is not well established.

genetic: No specific gene mutation identified; suspected autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
other: Histopathology: increased dense collagen bundles with decreased elastic fibers in dermis
Clinical examination: multiple firm dermal nodules

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of hypomelanotic macules, facial angiofibromas, and systemic involvement
Genetic testing positive for TSC1 or TSC2 mutations
Sudden onset of multiple collagenomas without family history
Lesions often appear in adolescence without autosomal dominant pattern
Connective tissue nevi with elastic tissue abnormalities

redFlags: Rapid increase in number or size of cutaneous nodules
Presence of systemic symptoms such as cardiac abnormalities
Family history of connective tissue disorders or syndromic features
references: Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
